name: Iran nuclear programme
summary: IAEA's Grossi tells board it cannot verify Iran's 60% uranium; no access at Fordow, Natanz or Isfahan
state: IAEA Director General Grossi told the agency's board in November that, apart from Bushehr, Iran has given neither information nor access at sites including Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan, and that the agency has lacked continuity of knowledge of uranium enriched up to 60% for nearly 18 months (La Voce di New York, 22 Nov). A 13 Nov IAEA report said it cannot rule out diversion of declared material and does not know where Iran's underground Isfahan enrichment plant is (The National). No strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or evidence of weaponisation was found to 23 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: No direct effect on daily life in the UK. Developments in Iran's nuclear programme can move oil prices and the risk of renewed strikes in the Gulf; travellers should follow FCDO travel advice for Iran and the region.
rubric_hit: Watch: inspector access curtailed; IAEA cannot verify Iran's uranium enriched up to 60% (Nov Board of Governors)

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
